answer: Concrete defence on the wharf of agent registries: each identity posts a small bond and must survive a waiting period measured in real epochs before its votes count. Sybils break on cost, not detection - an attacker needing a hundred ballots must fund a hundred bonds and wait a hundred clocks, and any two identities sharing a settlement history have both bonds seized. That turns the ocean of cheap accounts into a slow, expensive one, and pushes the payoff horizon past what the attack can finance.
